name: Evergreen Collaborative (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: shares of the result at the defaults. The public money the Inflation Reduction Act won for US households and the EPA rules' net compliance savings (7%) are in the United States; the tonnes (93%) spare people everywhere, spread by world population, the small US power-plant and vehicle smoke share left in the world figure.
summary: Evergreen Collaborative, the tax-deductible research and education arm of the Evergreen climate groups (its sister Evergreen Action, a 501(c)(4), does most of the lobbying), writes US federal and state clean-energy policy and makes the public case for it ($8.6M spent in 2024). This model counts its wins of 2021-2024 with published tonnes (the Inflation Reduction Act, Michigan's 2023 clean-energy laws and EPA's 2024 power-plant and vehicle standards), its other wins as a share, against the same years' spending. At the defaults that is 0.0026 years of healthy life per $1,000: a dollar given averts about 0.012 tonnes of CO₂e (about $80 a tonne), most of it through the federal law; each win is shared with hundreds of groups (Evergreen Collaborative is credited with 0.1% to 2% of the advocacy behind each) and with what would have happened anyway, and since 2025 the law's credits have been cut back and the EPA rules repealed. The biggest uncertainties are the discount rate, the missing-data discount and the years a won reform counts; every branch is discounted for missing data, since no tonne is measured for its work.

source.quote: helped mobilize over 1 million public comments urging strong standards

source.title: Evergreen Action, Our impact and wins
source.quote: policies first outlined in our Evergreen Action Plan

rows.explainer: Evergreen's two organisations made the law's clean-energy credits, grants and Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund their main asks in 2021-2022 (its 2022 return, Part III: two dozen papers and memos, 290 press citations), ran the No Climate, No Deal campaign and pushed to keep the climate money when the clean-electricity payment programme was dropped; the lobbying was mostly its 501(c)(4) sister's. Against all the groups, unions and industry behind the law (hundreds of millions of dollars a year), Evergreen Collaborative's $5.2M of spending in 2021-2022 is a small share, raised for its focus on the law and its early policy design. 0.4% (0.15% to 1.2%), our judgment: the Union of Concerned Scientists' 1% is for a programme about ten times larger with a smaller share of it on the law.

rows.label: Years of the larger home credits counted (the shared years a won reform counts, at most the years they paid)
Inflation Reduction Act's larger home credits: claimants' gain less taxpayers' cost, units of value
rows.explainer: The law's increase in the two home credits (25C, 25D; facts: climate.ira_home_credits_*), year by year over the years counted, valued as the claimants' gain less the taxpayers' cost and discounted from the first claims, as Rewiring America's model counts them.

rows.label: Inflation Reduction Act's home rebates and credits: Evergreen Collaborative's share of the advocacy behind them, relative to its share behind the whole law
rows.explainer: Evergreen's asks were the whole package of credits and grants, its buildings work among them, but the home rebates and credits were chiefly Rewiring America's and the solar industry's asks, so half its share of the whole law carries over to them (0.2 to 1), our judgment, as in the Union of Concerned Scientists' model. The tonnes keep the whole law's share.

rows.label: Public money won for households, units of value per year of the period (after the law's branch steps)
rows.formula: (ira_rebate_uov + ira_credit_uov) * ira_attribution_share * ira_household_focus_adj * p_success * ira_counterfactual_adj * missing_data_adj / period_years
rows.explainer: The law's branch steps for the money: advocacy's share of the win, Evergreen Collaborative's share of the advocacy behind the home provisions, what wouldn't have come anyway and the missing-data step, spread over the period's four years. The tonnes' evidence and delivery steps are left out, as in Rewiring America's model: the money is a sum in the statute and the claims Treasury counted, its delivery in the paid share.

rows.label: EPA power-plant standards: compliance costs, units of value (negative)
rows.formula: -@compliance_costs.us_power_plant_rule_2024_cost_per_year * @cpi.usa_2024 / @cpi.usa_2019 * $uov_per_ln_consumption / (@public_funds.compliance_cost_payer_multiple * @united_states.ce_expenditure_per_person_2024) * pwr_downstream / pwr_tonnes_per_year * pwr_counterfactual_adj * pwr_attribution_share * pwr_implementation_adj * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The won rule's compliance costs (docs/normalization.md 2.21): the power system's extra cost (EPA's regulatory impact analysis, $0.98 billion a year), in 2019 dollars moved to 2024's, valued as money lost by those who bear it, consumers and owners (@public_funds.compliance_cost_payer_multiple, 1.2 times average US consumption), on the log scale; over the same years and wait as the rule's benefits, with the branch's chance, counterfactual, credit, delivered share and missing-data step, not its evidence adjustment (which is about the benefits).

rows.label: EPA vehicle standards: compliance costs, units of value (negative)
rows.formula: -@compliance_costs.us_light_medium_vehicle_rule_2024_net_cost_per_year * @cpi.usa_2024 / @cpi.usa_2022 * $uov_per_ln_consumption / (@public_funds.compliance_cost_payer_multiple * @united_states.ce_expenditure_per_person_2024) * veh_downstream / veh_tonnes_per_year * veh_counterfactual_adj * veh_attribution_share * veh_implementation_adj * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The won rule's compliance costs (docs/normalization.md 2.21): buyers' technology, charger and insurance costs less their fuel, maintenance and repair savings (EPA's rule, a net saving of $11.3 billion a year, so this row adds value), in 2022 dollars moved to 2024's, valued as money lost by those who bear it, consumers and owners (@public_funds.compliance_cost_payer_multiple, 1.2 times average US consumption), on the log scale; over the same years and wait as the rule's benefits, with the branch's chance, counterfactual, credit, delivered share and missing-data step, not its evidence adjustment (which is about the benefits).

rows.label: Compliance costs of the won rules, units of value per year of the period
rows.explainer: The two EPA rules' compliance costs summed, per year of the period, in the main chain (docs/normalization.md 2.21). The Inflation Reduction Act's credits are public money, not a rule's compliance cost (its household money is netted of taxpayers' cost above). Michigan's laws have no regulator's cost analysis (the Senate Fiscal Agency's analysis gives none), so they have no row; sponsors' estimates claim bill savings.

rows.label: Units of value a year counted outside the tonnes: public money won for households and the rules' compliance costs
rows.explainer: The household money (recipients' gain less taxpayers' cost) plus the won rules' compliance costs (negative), the input of the bridge into tonnes.

rows.label: Evergreen Collaborative's share of the resources behind the wins (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.formula: (pwr_downstream * pwr_counterfactual_adj * pwr_attribution_share_shared + veh_downstream * veh_counterfactual_adj * veh_attribution_share_shared + ira_downstream * ira_counterfactual_adj * ira_attribution_share_shared + mi_downstream * mi_counterfactual_adj * mi_attribution_share_shared) / (pwr_downstream * pwr_counterfactual_adj + veh_downstream * veh_counterfactual_adj + ira_downstream * ira_counterfactual_adj + mi_downstream * mi_counterfactual_adj)

source.title: Evergreen Action, Our impact and wins
source.quote: Evergreen helped Pennsylvania secure nearly $400 million

rows.explainer: The four branches are Evergreen's wins of 2021-2024 with published tonnes; the rest, each a share of the modelled value: Pennsylvania's federal climate pollution reduction grant for heavy industry (about $400 million) and the national zero-emission freight corridor strategy, 7%; EPA's other power-sector rules it campaigned for (mercury and air toxics, coal ash, water discharge), 4%; its campaign that led utilities to leave a trade association over its lobbying, and its work for other states' clean-power laws, 4%. 15% (5% to 40%), our judgment, as in the Union of Concerned Scientists' model.

rows.label: All adjustments combined (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.formula: (pwr_downstream * pwr_total_adj + veh_downstream * veh_total_adj + ira_downstream * ira_total_adj + mi_downstream * mi_total_adj) / (pwr_downstream + veh_downstream + ira_downstream + mi_downstream)
rows.explainer: The branches' own combined adjustments apply; this is their average, weighted by each branch's expected tonnes before adjustments, for reading only.

rows.label: EPA power-plant standards: expected tonnes a year once in effect (weight for the fuel and methane shares)
EPA vehicle standards: expected tonnes a year once in effect (weight for the fuel and methane shares)
Inflation Reduction Act: expected tonnes a year once in effect (weight for the fuel and methane shares)
Michigan's clean-energy laws: expected tonnes a year once in effect (weight for the fuel and methane shares)
rows.explainer: Weighted before waits and years counted, as the other branches' expected tonnes.

rows.label: Share of these tonnes that are methane
rows.explainer: The Inflation Reduction Act's methane part (facts: climate.ira_methane_share_2030, 5%) of the expected tonnes, weighted before waits and years counted (which can't feed a conversion row); the other wins cut CO₂. The shared conversion values it by methane's own, earlier warming and ozone.

rows.label: Share of these tonnes from burning less fossil fuel near people
rows.formula: (pwr_expected_tonnes + veh_expected_tonnes + ira_expected_tonnes + mi_expected_tonnes - ira_expected_tonnes * @climate.ira_methane_share_2030) / (pwr_expected_tonnes + veh_expected_tonnes + ira_expected_tonnes + mi_expected_tonnes)
rows.explainer: Every tonne here except the act's methane is fuel burned less near people: power plants, cars, and clean power displacing coal and gas.

rows.label: Air-pollution deaths per tonne of these fuel tonnes, relative to the fossil-fuel average
rows.formula: (pwr_expected_tonnes * @climate.us_coal_power_smoke_factor + veh_expected_tonnes * @climate.us_vehicle_smoke_factor + ira_expected_tonnes * (1 - @climate.ira_methane_share_2030) * (@climate.ira_power_share_2030 * @climate.us_power_smoke_factor + (1 - @climate.ira_power_share_2030) * @climate.us_vehicle_smoke_factor) + mi_expected_tonnes * @climate.us_power_smoke_factor) / (pwr_expected_tonnes + veh_expected_tonnes + ira_expected_tonnes * (1 - @climate.ira_methane_share_2030) + mi_expected_tonnes)
rows.explainer: Per fuel and place, weighted by expected fuel tonnes: the power-plant standards' tonnes are coal plants' (facts: climate.us_coal_power_smoke_factor), the vehicle rules' cars' (climate.us_vehicle_smoke_factor), the Inflation Reduction Act's by sector (climate.ira_power_share_2030: electricity at US power's factor, the rest at cars'), and Michigan's laws' US power's (climate.us_power_smoke_factor: the standard displaces the state's remaining coal and gas).

rows.label: Air pollution these tonnes cut, relative to an average fossil-fuel tonne
rows.explainer: Read by the tco2e unit's conversion (docs/normalization.md 2.5).

rows.label: Air-pollution deaths averted per tonne, counted directly (none here)

rows.formula: uov_counted_per_year / (($deaths_per_tco2e * $climate_heat_share * ((1 - methane_share) * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -$climate_heat_death_delay + methane_share * @climate.methane_heat_deaths_vs_co2 * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -@climate.methane_heat_death_delay) * (1 + @climate.nondeath_damages_vs_deaths) * (@death_ages.heat_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.heat_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.heat_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.heat_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74) + ($deaths_per_tco2e * (1 - $climate_heat_share) * air_pollution_weight + extra_deaths_per_tco2e + methane_share * @climate.ozone_deaths_per_tco2e_methane / (1 + ln(1 + $discount_rate) * @climate.methane_lifetime_years)) * (@death_ages.air_pollution_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74)) * $life_value_multiplier)
rows.explainer: The households' gain and the won rules' compliance costs (uov_counted_per_year) enter the tonnes only through the site's fixed bridge (docs/normalization.md 2.6): they move with the value of consumption, not with the climate sliders.

rows.label: Tonnes of CO₂e averted per year of the period
rows.formula: (pwr_downstream * pwr_total_adj + veh_downstream * veh_total_adj + ira_downstream * ira_total_adj + mi_downstream * mi_total_adj) / period_years * (1 + unmodelled_benefits_adj) + tco2e_from_uov
rows.explainer: Each win's expected tonnes × its own adjustments, summed, spread over the period's four years, with the other wins added as a share, plus the public money won for households and the rules' compliance costs in tonnes.
